item.title: C Language Argument Promotion Rules: Prototypes vs Non-Prototypes
item.description:
“C Language Argument Promotion Rules: Prototypes vs Non-Prototypes”

C Function Argument Promotion Rules: Prototype Presence Matters

When a function is defined or called, the handling of its parameters depends heavily on the existence of a function prototype.

Non-Variadic Functions with Prototypes

If a function is declared or defined with a prototype, parameters passed must match the declared type. Any type smaller than int (like char or short) is implicitly converted to its corresponding promoted type, which is typically int. Similarly, float is promoted to double.
